production.note: US model years 1965-1967 (the task's US years; no opened page states US model years). Build dates: "Jaguar built 12,583 examples of the 4.2-litre Series 1 between October 1964 and July 1967". The later 'Series 1.5' (from August 1967, US cars with Stromberg carburettors and 245 bhp per this page) is not covered.

body.note: Fixed Head Coupe (FHC) and Open Two Seater (OTS); the OTS has a fixed-roof sibling, so it is 'Convertible'. The 2+2 coupe (from 1966) is a longer-wheelbase car and is not described by these figures.

configuration.note: Dual overhead cam straight six (XK engine)

displacementL.note: 4,235 cc: "displacement went from 3781cc to 4235cc". Classic & Sports Car: "4235cc 'six'".

aspiration.note: Triple SU carburettors; no forced induction

drivetrain.note: "four-speed manual or (2+2 only) three-speed auto, RWD"

transmission.note: "four-speed manual or (2+2 only) three-speed auto, RWD"; the automatic was 2+2 only, so the coupe and OTS had the 4-speed manual. Supercar Nostalgia: "Jaguar's own full-synchromesh unit".

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (publication outside the major list, plus an enthusiast site). Jaguar's rating, an SAE gross figure per the batch rule for pre-1980 cars; neither page names the standard. Quote (Classic & Sports Car, Malcolm McKay, spec panel): "265bhp @ 5400rpm". Quote (Supercar Nostalgia): "While the 4.2-litre engine produced the same headline 265bhp as before, this was now delivered at 5400rpm as opposed to 5500rpm." The automobile-catalog search-result title for the US 1967 4.2 XK-E Coupe also gives "265 hp (for North America U.S.)" (automobile-catalog-xke-42-coupe-1967; page itself refused the fetch).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (single enthusiast source). Fixed Head Coupe, 1,232 kg x 2.20462 = 2,716 lb; the OTS is 1,219 kg (2,687 lb). Quote: "Weight was officially unchanged from the outgoing 3.8 (1219kg for the OTS Roadster and 1232kg for the FHC)." The page does not say whether this is a kerb or dry figure, nor which market. Classic & Sports Car's panel gives only a range for all S1-S2 E-types, "2688-3192lb (1197-1422kg)", which contains this figure.

reviewNotes: Weight basis unknown: the only specific figure (1,232 kg FHC, Supercar Nostalgia, described as 'officially' unchanged from the 3.8) is not labelled kerb or dry and not tied to the US market. A readable Jaguar US brochure or a period US road-test spec panel should confirm both power (265 bhp SAE gross) and weight. auto-brochures.com's 1965 US E-Type brochure is a scanned PDF with no readable text.
provisionalNote: Power (265 hp SAE gross) rests on Classic & Sports Car's spec panel (not a major-list magazine) and Supercar Nostalgia, agreeing. Weight (2,716 lb, FHC) rests on a single enthusiast page (1,232 kg, kerb/dry and market not stated). A Jaguar US brochure or a major magazine's spec panel for the 1965-67 4.2 coupe would replace both.
